subject: BCP KV cache drift — witness log & RPO attestation
messages:
From: Priya Verma <pverma@fincloud.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: KV cache drift witness & RPO attestation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As part of FinCloud's vendor SIG/CAIQ refresh, the security and resilience team asked us to collect a short set of artifacts and schedule a live witness for your KV cache warm-start behavior. Specifically they want: 

- A short witness session (30–45m) where we observe a warm-start after failover (or simulated failover) and confirm TTL/kv-prefix consistency.
- Recent KV snapshot and replay traces showing the last warm-start and the prefix reconciliation timeline.
- Measured RTO (time-to-serve) for the primary path and fallback, and RPO evidence (eg. kv-snapshots + sequence IDs).
- Your runbook excerpt that documents the warm-start steps and point-in-time recovery checks.

Attached is our standard ask doc (FinCloud_BCP_ask_20261210.pdf) with the specific SIG questions called out. We'd like to schedule the witness on Mon, Dec 21 between 10:30–13:30 PST. Can you confirm availability and what artifacts you can provide ahead of time?

If it helps, Jordan flagged that Ben on your ops team may have the snapshots.

Thanks,
Priya Verma
Security Risk Manager
FinCloud

Attachments: FinCloud_BCP_ask_20261210.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Verma <pverma@fincloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: KV cache drift witness & RPO attestation

Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can provide everything requested and run the witness on Mon 12/21. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Pre-witness bundle (to you by EOD Sun): 
   - KV snapshot of latest state (CSV) + sequence id mapping
   - Replay trace (log) showing cache warm-up timeline and timestamps
   - Excerpt of operational runbook showing the warm-start checklist (runbook-v2.pdf clip)
   - Measured metrics from our last tabletop (RTO, RPO) and a short explanation of how we measure them

2) Witness session: live failover simulation in a sandbox; demonstrate warm-start and show the live timeline. We'll also show a short trace that proves the RPO bound (how we rehydrate prefix keys).

3) Post-witness: Attestation email and CSV of raw timings.

Ben, Jordan — can you pull the 12/18 kv snapshot and replay trace and drop into the shared Drive folder listed below? I attached a quick checklist to show the items Priya expects.

Thanks — I'll lock the witness time once Priya confirms.

—Rishi
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rishi_initial_checklist.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: KV snapshot + replay traces (12/18)

Rishi / Jordan,

I pulled the artifacts from the staging exercise we ran on 2026-12-18 and uploaded them to the shared folder. Quick summary: 

- kv-snapshot-20261218.csv: contains key, prefix-id, sequence-id, and last-write-ts (UTC). Snapshot taken at 2026-12-18T23:54:12Z.
- replay-trace-20261218.log: trace shows warm-start sequence; key hydration begins at 2026-12-18T23:55:18Z and completes at 2026-12-18T23:55:42Z (approx 24s wall-clock for the observed dataset).
- runbook-v2.pdf (excerpt): warm-start checklist, owner oncall, and recovery verifications (step 4 includes a KV prefix reconciliation verification).

Measured numbers from that exercise (staging):
- Observed RTO (application-serving latency after failover): median 7m 12s (measurement window: 5 trials).
- Observed RPO: effectively <30s in our test because warm cache uses sequence-id rehydration and prefix replay. We include sequence-id mapping in the snapshot to prove it.

Notes/caveats: production datasets are larger — the warm-start time scales with the hot-key working set and our batching configuration. For the witness we can run a targeted warm-start for a customer-sized keyspace to show representative timings.

I've attached the CSV/logs here for the pack.

Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-snapshot-20261218.csv, replay-trace-20261218.log, runbook-v2.pdf

From: Priya Verma <pverma@fincloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: FinCloud Security <security@fincloud.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 12:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: KV cache drift witness & RPO attestation

Thanks Rishi and Ben — received and that looks good.

We can do the witness on Mon 2026-12-21 at 11:00 PST. Agenda: 5–10m intro, 20–25m live failover/warm-start demo, 10m Q&A and wrap. Please include the following in the pre-witness bundle: 

- A one-page summary (PDF) with the test objective, RTO/RPO numbers and any assumptions (env size, dataset footprint)
- Contact list of personnel who will be present and their roles
- Shared Drive link with the artifacts (we have access to the link you referenced below)

Ben, can you confirm the snapshot timestamp and that the replay trace contains the sequence-id mapping? Also please ensure the runbook excerpt includes the checklist step numbers (security needs the step ids for their CAIQ reference).

I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm the attendees.

Best,
Priya Verma
Security Risk Manager
FinCloud
